children: , the Chinese commerce and cloud-AI giant, landed in an unexpected place: a Federal Register search tool powered by its Qwen AI model. The U.S. shares jumped approximately 4.3% to $113.25 Friday morning. The valuation picture adds another angle: at $113.25, Alibaba trades 5.76% below its GF Value estimate of $120.17.

The Qwen-powered search option was available Wednesday before disappearing around the time social-media posts drew attention to it. Reuters reported that the FBI recently accused Alibaba of copying technology from Anthropic, an allegation the Chinese embassy in Washington called unfounded. The immediate cybersecurity concern appeared limited because the Federal Register deals with public information, but experts said the bigger question is whether any U.S. government data traveled outside federal systems.

That distinction matters for Alibaba investors. Qwen is open-weight, so organizations can download and operate the model on their own infrastructure rather than sending everything back to Alibaba. That makes distribution easier and potentially cheaper, but adoption inside sensitive institutions can still collide with procurement rules and U.S.-China technology tensions. Qwen can spread without Alibaba controlling every deployment; turning that reach into durable institutional acceptance is the harder part.

title: Alibaba Jumps 4.3% With Qwen's Brief U.S. Government Appearance
